items.claim: Non-finite `fadeMs` accepted, then thrown from the middle of a later edit
items.note: I also refuse a negative `fadeMs`. That is my own strict call, and it is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `replace` with the def already in place, or one def added under two ids, disposes a live def
items.note: `add`, `replace` and `apply` now throw on any def the graph holds or has held, as the insert chain already does for effects. `replace(id, sameDef)` throws rather than doing nothing. That is my own strict call, and it is recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `settled()` resolves while a connect's or a replace's fade-in is still ramping
A non-looping file stopped between its natural end and its `ended` event never rewinds, so the next start is silent
A source whose `start` throws stays marked running, and the `start`, `add` or `replace` is left half done
items.note: Each of those calls now changes nothing when a source's start throws.

items.claim: `createOscillatorNode` accepts a non-finite `frequency` and throws only at the next start
`createEdits` went past check:size's 120-line function cap after the fixes above
items.note: by moving the busy test and the `add` rollback into helpers.

items.claim: `createInsertChain` takes a non-finite `fadeMs` the same way (`packages/audio/src/inserts.ts:86`, raised by A)
items.note: not fixed. It is outside `audio.graph`, and the fixer for the inserts area could edit the same line.

items.claim: Non-finite `fadeMs` accepted, edits on a running context fail partway
items.note: The graph now throws `RangeError` at construction on a `fadeMs` that is not finite or is below 0. Refusing a negative value is my call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: A def whose `start` throws stops the sources after it from starting, and its node stays marked running
items.note: `createOscillatorNode` now refuses a non-finite `frequency` when it is built. A source whose `start` throws is no longer marked running, `start()` starts the rest and then rethrows, and `apply` carries on past it the way it does past a throwing `set`. While fixing this I found that a `replace` whose new source throws on start skipped closing the old def's faders, which left the graph busy forever; it now closes them first. Keeping the node in the graph after its failed start is my call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `settled()` resolves while a new connection is still fading in
items.note: A fader now tracks its open ramp, and `busy()` counts it until the ramp lands.

items.claim: A non-looping file stopped after its natural end comes back silent on the next start
items.note: The playhead now restarts a non-looping buffer that reached its end from offset 0.

items.claim: `replace(id, def)` with the def already live, or one still fading out, disposes the live def
items.note: `add` and `replace` now throw on any def the graph still holds, and `apply` refuses one before changing anything. The same mistake existed in `add`, where a def shared with another node was double-held, so it is refused too. Refusing a retrigger with the same def is my call, recorded in `docs/unruled.md`.
